statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 6 (low) with Nasdaq-100 futures inside the CME weekend halt, against Stress 54 (elevated) after Washington rejected Iran's seven-day Strait of Hormuz roadmap, with Friday's close leaving the ten-year Treasury yield near a two-decade high at 5.18% and an October Fed hike priced as more likely than not.
recommendation: Tail stays in a 6-9 band and far below the 25 blocking threshold in every assessed hour, so the mapped policy state is EA_ON across the whole window. No danger window is published: a market that does not trade cannot supply the observed price-path evidence a narrow evidence-based window requires, and the CME reopen at 22:00Z on Sunday falls four hours beyond the end of this forecast. Elevated Stress describes a difficult environment that may still mean-revert and is reported separately from the Tail-derived state.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 6 while the rejected Hormuz roadmap and a 5.18% ten-year lift Stress to 54
body: Nasdaq-100 futures have been halted since Friday's 21:00Z settlement and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, four hours after this forecast window closes, so every assessed hour is structurally incapable of containing an observed price path. Friday's completed session argues against pathological structure rather than for it: NDX closed at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and about 0.53% below its 52-week high of 30,770.63, with VIX down 5.11% to 14.87 while the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite all booked weekly gains of 0.3%, 1.2% and 2% despite the bond sell-off. That is a two-way auction closing away from both extremes, so Tail is held at 6. Stress is a separate question and edges to 54. The Strait of Hormuz remains closed on day 210 after President Trump rejected Tehran's seven-day reopening roadmap on Saturday, saying the deal would not be acceptable; Iran had asked for the naval blockade lifted, oil sanctions waived, roughly $12bn in frozen assets released and a regional ceasefire observed, and offered nuclear inspections, while President Pezeshkian said Iran has no trust in the American side. Reporting that the administration privately expects renewed strikes after the November midterms adds a slow-burn escalation premium. Energy is nonetheless discounting the closure rather than pricing escalation: WTI fell 2.33% to 92.41 for a roughly 7.4% weekly loss and Brent eased 2.24% to 104.32, with IMF PortWatch recording one transit on 20 September against an 85-a-day baseline. The rate path compounds the environment: the official H.15 series for 24 September shows 4.87% at two years, 5.18% at ten and 5.47% at thirty, a near two-decade high at the long end that Fed Chair Kevin Warsh attributes to economic strength, and market pricing puts an October hike in the low-to-mid 60s percent with December less firmly priced. The thirty-year fixed mortgage reached 7.45%, its highest in more than two years. Shared latest-session context was mildly constructive beneath the surface, with megacaps 6 of 8 higher on a 3.66% Microsoft gain against a 3.33% Meta decline and semiconductors 6 of 7 higher, but that collection was 121 minutes old, beyond its 90-minute freshness bound, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it cannot establish current structure. Confidence of 79 reflects verified index, volatility, yield, energy and calendar evidence, discounted for the structurally absent live tape, the stale and partial shared context, and minor disagreement between sources on the precise October hike probability.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, so none is unavailable. The window opens in the closing hours of Friday's U.S. cash session, where Tail ran 18-19 with EA_ON mapped throughout and Stress held in the mid-50s under a mixed mode. After Friday's 21:00Z futures settlement Tail decayed from 12 to 8 and Stress eased from 50 into the mid-40s as the session's directional question closed out and the mode moved to normal. Through Saturday the halt kept Tail flat at 7-8 while Stress rebuilt from 44 to 53 as the Hormuz diplomacy deteriorated, and Confidence drifted from the high 80s to 80-83 as the last tradable tape aged. No hour in the window was mapped above green, and no historical opinion has been restated using later information.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forecast hours falls inside the CME weekend halt, which runs until 22:00Z on Sunday, four hours past the end of this window, so no hour can contain observed price-path structure. Tail is held in a 6-9 band throughout and stays far below the 25 blocking threshold, mapping EA_ON and green in every slot. The step from 6 to 7 at the start of Sunday and to 8 and then 9 through Sunday afternoon is accumulated unpriced gap risk ahead of a single reopening auction, not observed one-way structure. Stress traces the weekend news-flow windows, easing to 49 in the thin overnight hours and building to 56 late on Sunday on the unresolved strait closure, Brent near 104 and a rate path pricing an October hike. Confidence decays from 79 to 72 purely because the newest observable tape ages past 42 hours with no replacement possible before the reopen. The conditional branch that would matter is the shape of that reopen: an orderly two-way auction with genuine retracement would validate the low Tail carried here, while immediate one-way extension holding near an extreme would be the first real amplifier.
